facts: Santiago is a young shepherd in Andalusia, Spain, who had chosen to travel with his sheep rather than become a priest as his parents wished.
He has the same dream twice: a child leads him to the Egyptian pyramids and tells him he will find a hidden treasure there.
He asks a gypsy woman to interpret it; she tells him to go to the pyramids and asks for a tenth of the treasure as payment.

An old man appears who reveals himself as Melchizedek, the king of Salem. He tells Santiago about his 'Personal Legend', what he has always wanted to accomplish, and says that when you truly want something, the whole universe conspires to help you achieve it.
The king asks for a tenth of Santiago's sheep and gives him two stones, Urim and Thummim, to help read omens.
Santiago sells his flock and crosses to Tangier in Africa, where on his first day he is robbed of all his money.
tension: Santiago has a secure, contented life with his sheep, and the only reason to give it up is a dream he had twice.
opening_idea: Start with a shepherd who knows each of his sheep, and a dream about treasure at the pyramids that comes back a second time.

lessons.idea: Following a calling usually means giving up something comfortable and concrete for something uncertain.
lessons.anchor: Santiago sells the flock he knows for a dream about distant pyramids.

lessons.idea: Committing to a path doesn't protect you from setbacks; the first step can go wrong immediately.
lessons.anchor: On his first day in Tangier, Santiago is robbed of all his money.

reflect: Is there something you've wanted to do for a long time that keeps coming back to you, like a recurring dream?
What 'flock' would you have to sell to go after it?
reflect_final: Name one thing you've long wanted to try, and choose one small step you can take this week that costs something real but not everything.

use_cases.situation: You keep postponing a long-held plan, such as learning an instrument or starting a side project.
use_cases.move: Santiago didn't sell his sheep until the dream came twice; write down how many times you've come back to this idea, then book one concrete first step for this week.

use_cases.situation: Your teenager talks about a dream career that sounds impractical.
use_cases.move: Ask what first step they could try in the next month, instead of debating whether the dream is realistic.

use_cases.situation: A friend says they'd love to change careers 'someday.'
use_cases.move: Ask what their equivalent of the sheep is: the thing they'd have to let go of first, and whether a smaller version exists.

pocket_idea: Santiago had to sell his sheep before he could look for treasure: a Personal Legend usually starts by giving up something you already have.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A shepherd sold his whole flock because he had the same dream twice, and was robbed on his very first day abroad.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd, dreams twice of treasure at the pyramids; an old king tells him about his Personal Legend, he sells his sheep, sails to Tangier, and loses all his money on day one.
conversation_variants.question_idea: Is there an idea that keeps coming back to you, the way Santiago's dream did?
conversation_variants.key_contrast_idea: The safety of a life you know versus the pull of something you've always wanted to do.
